Root cause of the originally-cited '_N vs _vN unresolved reference' and 'offset_from receiver/signedness' bugs: three CIR ops -- lower_ptr_stride, lower_ptr_diff, and the array-decay-to-integer arm of lower_cast -- called operand_expr() (which only resolves self.values/self.slots) on a pointer-typed base that was actually an ElementPtr/MemberPtr fact (never materialized into self.values), or applied no cast at all when a pointer decayed to a plain integer result type. Fixed by:
  - lower_ptr_stride/lower_ptr_diff: use pointer_operand_expr() instead of operand_expr() for pointer-typed operands, so element/member place facts resolve to a real std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(...) expression instead of falling through to a bare, unresolved SSA-name identifier.
  - lower_cast: two related ptrtoint bugs found and fixed in the same investigation -- (1) a Global operand cast to a non-pointer result type was passed through unresolved as Val::Global, which a later to_expr() rendered as a bare read of the global's VALUE (e.g. '(long)&g1 % 512' became 'g1 % 512', silently reading g1's stored contents instead of its address); (2) a local array slot decaying to a non-pointer (integer) result type produced '.as_mut_ptr()' with no enclosing cast, which doesn't type-check against an integer-typed destination. Both now correctly emit 'std::ptr::addr_of!(name) as T' / '(x.as_mut_ptr() as T)'.

Root cause: Clang CIR hoists all local allocas to a function's entry block, reusing generic compiler names (e.g. 'tmp') across distinct temps such as per-GNU-statement-expression result slots. lower_alloca took the CIR name verbatim, so colliding allocas produced repeated 'let mut tmp = ...' bindings that Rust resolved to the last (differently-typed) shadow, causing widespread i32/u64 call-site mismatches. Fixed by deduping local names per function in src/lower.rs (declared_local_names + unique_local_name).
